confidence_note: Written from memory of the book's fear-setting exercise and secondary summaries; book text not opened. The three questions (define the nightmare; what could you do to repair or recover; the cost of doing nothing) and the 1, 5, 10 year frame are remembered, medium confidence on the exact timeframes. Old TR text errors: it says Ferriss runs the exercise 'before every decision' and gives a '5 years' wording as 'the strongest question'; the book's own frame is the cost of inaction over several horizons, and the name 'fear-setting' is Ferriss's. The paraphrase 'most people choose unhappiness over uncertainty' and 'what we fear doing most is usually what we most need to do' are the book's, medium confidence; used as paraphrase, not as quotes. No personal anecdote of Ferriss included (not verified). Concept story: no invented protagonist.
facts: Ferriss calls the exercise 'fear-setting': write down the thing you are afraid to do and then work it through on paper.
Step one: define the nightmare, the worst that could realistically happen if you did it.
Step two: write what you could do to repair the damage or get back on your feet, even temporarily.
Step three: write the cost of not acting, in emotional, physical and financial terms, over a year, five years and ten years.
Ferriss's observation: what we fear doing most is usually what we most need to do; and people tend to choose unhappiness over uncertainty.
scene_details: A page with the nightmare written out in full
A list of ways to recover set beside it
The same page extended to the cost of doing nothing at one, five and ten years
tension: Fear of acting is loud and specific; the cost of not acting is quiet and never written down.
opening_idea: Open on the page itself: the worst case in full on one side, the cost of doing nothing on the other.

lessons.idea: Put the cost of staying put on the same page as the cost of trying, so the comparison is fair.
lessons.anchor: Step three of fear-setting asks what inaction costs at one, five and ten years.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: Someone who delays a hard conversation with a landlord lists what the delay costs each month.

reflect_final: What decision are you putting off, and what has it already cost you in time, money or peace of mind?

use_cases.situation: You are afraid to ask for a raise.
use_cases.move: Write the worst response, how you would recover, and what staying silent costs in a year.

use_cases.situation: A friend is stuck on a decision.
use_cases.move: Ask them to write what happens if nothing changes in five years.

use_cases.situation: You are hesitating on a career move.
use_cases.move: Take twenty minutes tonight to write the three steps on one page.

pocket_idea: Write the cost of doing nothing next to your worst case, because fear only ever draws one side.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Ferriss's fear exercise adds a column most people forget: what staying put costs.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Ferriss's fear-setting is three questions on paper. What is the worst that could happen if I do it? What could I do to recover? And what does doing nothing cost me over one, five and ten years? Most people only ever work through the first.
